## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

ProfileRepository — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/profile/ProfileRepository.kt (interface), implemented by core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/profile/ProfileRepositoryImpl.kt

## Trigger

A ViewModel or controller method calling into the repository directly
from a UI event handler, outside `viewModelScope.launch` — e.g.
`ProfileViewModel.onHrMaxUpdated` (app-phone/.../ui/profile/ProfileViewModel.kt)
calling `profileRepository.updateHrMaxBpm(value)` synchronously on the
calling (UI) thread — observed.

## Today

None of `ProfileRepository`'s methods are `suspend`.
`ProfileRepositoryImpl.currentOrDefault` (core-data/.../profile/ProfileRepositoryImpl.kt)
wraps `profileDao.observe().first()` in `runBlocking`, and every
updater (`updateHrMaxBpm`, `updateZoneThreshold`, `updateExpectedDistanceM`,
`updateLongPressMs`, `updateCorrectionFactor`, `markSyncSuccess`) calls
`currentOrDefault()` then `profileDao.upsert(...)` synchronously — both
on whatever thread the caller is on. `ProfileDao` (core-data/.../db/ProfileDao.kt)
declares `observe()` and `upsert()` with no `suspend`. `ProfileViewModel.onHrMaxUpdated`,
`.onExpectedDistanceChanged`, `.onLongPressChanged` and
`.onZoneThresholdChanged` call these updaters directly from a UI event
handler, not inside `viewModelScope.launch`, so the Room write and the
hidden `runBlocking` read both happen on the caller's own thread — the
UI thread when reached from a Compose callback, matching the freeze
symptom named by the gap.

The same defect, independently confirmed, also holds for three other
interfaces named by the gap:
- `RaceRepository` (core-domain/.../race/RaceRepository.kt):
  no method is `suspend`; `RaceRepositoryImpl` (core-data/.../race/RaceRepositoryImpl.kt)
  calls `RaceDao` (core-data/.../db/RaceDao.kt, itself entirely
  non-`suspend`) synchronously in every method — `setAsReference`,
  `rename`, `delete`, `saveImportedRace`, `saveRecordedRace`,
  `observeAll`, `findById`, `observeReference`, `replaceReference`.
  Called directly from `RaceDetailViewModel.setAsReference/rename/delete`
  and `ImportPreviewViewModel`, outside `viewModelScope.launch`.
- `WatchHistoryStore` (core-domain/.../sync/WatchHistoryStore.kt):
  `replaceAll` and `observe` are not `suspend`; `WatchHistoryStoreImpl`
  (core-data/.../sync/WatchHistoryStoreImpl.kt) calls `RaceHistoryDao.replaceAll`
  (non-`suspend`) synchronously.
- `RaceRecordingRepository` (core-domain/.../race/RaceRecordingRepository.kt):
  no method is `suspend`. Its implementation
  (app-wear/.../race/RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.kt) is in-memory, not
  Room-backed, but `markSegment` calls
  `runBlocking { profileRepository.observe().first() }` to read the
  correction factor — hiding a blocking wait on `ProfileRepository`'s
  own (equally synchronous) Room-backed flow. `markSegment` is called
  from `SegmentMarkingController.onPressEnd`, itself called directly
  from `MainRacePageViewModel.onPressEnd` and
  `ProjectionViewModel.onPressEnd` on a touch-release callback,
  matching the freeze symptom exactly.

The gap's wider claim does not hold for the other interfaces it names.
`ExerciseSessionSystem` (app-wear/.../sensor/session/ExerciseSessionSystem.kt)
already declares `availableDataTypes()` and `startExerciseSession()` as
`suspend`, and `ExerciseSessionManager` (app-wear/.../sensor/session/ExerciseSessionManager.kt)
already declares `open()` and `isDataTypeAvailable()` as `suspend` —
only `close()` and `onInteractivityChanged()`, which call
non-blocking, fire-and-forget Health Services calls, are not.
`CapabilitySource` (core-sync/.../link/WearableLinkStateSource.kt)
already declares `localNodeId()` and `reachableNodeIds()` as `suspend`.
`ConnectivityPermissionSystem` and `SensorPermissionSystem` already
declare `requestPermission()` — the one call that shows a dialog and
must suspend — as `suspend`; their `isGranted()`, `canShowSystemPrompt()`
and `openAppSettings()` wrap fast, non-blocking OS checks.
`ConnectivityPermissionLaunchStore` and `SensorPermissionLaunchStore`
are backed by `SharedPreferences` (ConnectivityPermissionLaunchStoreImpl,
SensorPermissionLaunchStoreImpl), read via `getBoolean` and written via
`.edit().putBoolean(...).apply()` — `apply()` is asynchronous by
design and `getBoolean` is the standard main-thread-safe access
pattern; neither blocks. `HapticFeedback`, `AmbientBinder` and `Clock`
wrap `Vibrator.vibrate()`, an ambient-lifecycle callback registration,
and `Instant.now()` respectively — none of these block a thread
waiting on another.

## Expected

`ProfileRepository`'s methods become `suspend`;
`ProfileRepositoryImpl` switches to `Dispatchers.IO` for its DAO calls
(replacing the hidden `runBlocking` in `currentOrDefault` with a plain
suspend read) and applies `flowOn(Dispatchers.IO)` to `observe()`.
`ProfileDao`'s non-Flow methods (`upsert`) become `suspend`. Every
direct caller — `ProfileViewModel.onHrMaxUpdated`,
`.onExpectedDistanceChanged`, `.onLongPressChanged`,
`.onZoneThresholdChanged` — moves its call inside `viewModelScope.launch`,
since a `suspend` call can no longer be made from a plain function.

The same change is a second gap on each of the following, each its own
symbol:
- `RaceRepository` (core-domain/.../race/RaceRepository.kt) and
  `RaceRepositoryImpl` (core-data/.../race/RaceRepositoryImpl.kt): every
  method becomes `suspend`, `RaceDao` calls move to `Dispatchers.IO`,
  `observeAll`/`observeReference` carry `flowOn(Dispatchers.IO)`.
  `RaceDetailViewModel.setAsReference/rename/delete` and
  `ImportPreviewViewModel.saveImportedRace` move their calls inside
  `viewModelScope.launch`.
- `WatchHistoryStore` (core-domain/.../sync/WatchHistoryStore.kt) and
  `WatchHistoryStoreImpl` (core-data/.../sync/WatchHistoryStoreImpl.kt):
  `replaceAll` becomes `suspend` and switches dispatcher; `observe()`
  carries `flowOn(Dispatchers.IO)`.
- `RaceRecordingRepository` (core-domain/.../race/RaceRecordingRepository.kt)
  and `RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl` (app-wear/.../race/RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.kt):
  `markSegment` becomes `suspend` and replaces its `runBlocking` call
  into `profileRepository.observe().first()` with a plain suspend
  call, now that `ProfileRepository.observe()` runs off the calling
  thread; `startClock`, `undoLastMark`, `stopRace`, `markSent` and
  `eraseRecorded` become `suspend` for consistency with the interface's
  in-process synchronization. This ripples to every caller of
  `markSegment`: `SegmentMarkingController.onPressEnd`
  (app-wear/.../race/SegmentMarkingController.kt) becomes `suspend`,
  and its own callers — `MainRacePageViewModel.onPressEnd` and
  `ProjectionViewModel.onPressEnd` — move their call inside
  `viewModelScope.launch`. `UndoMarkingController.undo`,
  `StopRaceController` and `RaceLaunchController` likewise wrap their
  now-`suspend` calls to `RaceRecordingRepository` in their own
  caller's `viewModelScope.launch`.

The four permission contracts, `ExerciseSessionSystem`,
`ExerciseSessionManager`, `HapticFeedback`, `AmbientBinder`,
`CapabilitySource` and `Clock` are not part of this fix — confirmed
already correct or non-blocking where the gap claims otherwise (see
Today).
